thread:
mike: quick sync — we need to pick between auth adaptors (inline in query service) vs proxy sidecar for RBAC enforcement. leaning toward adaptor for perf but worried about coupling and rollout complexity. anyone seen sharp tradeoffs we should care about?

anya: adaptor = lower p99s usually since no extra hop, easier to reuse runtime context (kv cache, token). downside is every language impl needs it and we mix auth code into query path.

sophia: proxy sidecar is nice for isolation and uniform metrics, plus can be swapped out without touching services. but it adds an extra network hop and complicates batching (we currently rely on same-proc batching).

raj: security notes — sidecar makes HSM/KMS attestation and auditing simpler (single place to integrate). adaptor can still call KMS but proliferation increases blast radius. also consider token translation complexity for impersonation flows.

anya: performance numbers from the last experiment: adaptor added ~0.2ms median, ~0.7ms p99; sidecar added ~1ms median, ~3-4ms p99 (cold). that extra p99 could matter for small interactive dashboards.

mike: thanks. other operational tradeoffs? like rollout strategies, circuit breaking, fallback?

sophia: adaptor rollout easier for canary by versioning the query service. sidecar requires infra rollout (daemonset / sidecar-injector) which is noisy for Dedicated clusters. but sidecar can be feature-flagged via envoy route too.

anya: we also need graceful fallback if auth service is down. adaptor can short-circuit to fallback cache with local TTL. sidecar would need a network fallback path or accept failure; both need careful SLO alignment.

raj: auditing: sidecar centralizes logs and makes compliance queries simpler. adaptor requires distributed traces and a log collector that stitches requests — doable but extra engineering.

mike: proposed compromise: start with adaptors in console-renderer and small query frontends where latency matters, keep sidecar pattern as blueprint for tenants that require strict isolation (private deployments). then gradually extract common auth library + shared gRPC interface so adaptors call a local auth-worker process (lightweight inproc or unix-socket) to get some isolation.

anya: +1. that hybrid gives us low-latency path for PLG-hosted users, and a clean migration path to sidecar for Dedicated/private. we should spell out migration steps.

sophia: migration checklist idea: 1) add auth adaptor interface & tests; 2) implement adaptor for console-query (go) + unit tests; 3) add feature flag to enable adaptor per service; 4) create auth-worker shim (unix socket) that adaptors can call; 5) run canaries (5% traffic) with latency and error SLIs; 6) iterate logs/traces; 7) offer sidecar deployment chart for customers who opt-in.

mike: can we get quick config snippet for the adaptor feature flag so infra can wire it into deploys?

anya: sure — simple example (k8s helm values):
```yaml
consoleQuery:
  auth:
    mode: "adaptor" # adaptor | sidecar
    featureFlag: "auth-adaptor-v1"
    adaptorConfig:
      cacheTTLms: 200
      workerSocket: "/tmp/auth-worker.sock"
```

mike: perfect. actionable items?

anya: i'll open RFC follow-up with perf numbers + unit tests and add a CANARY playbook. target: land adaptor in console-query canary next week.

raj: i'll draft the compliance note for sidecar requirements for Dedicated customers and enumerate KMS/HSM needs.

sophia: i'll own the auth-worker shim prototype and perf harness.
